newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares rally to set new record close.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares rally to set new record close.

text.p: Dutch shares rallied to fresh highs on Friday, with both main share indices setting a record close as market players revelled in a row of positive factors.
Various broker upgrades, market rumours, a stronger dollar, a supportive bond market and benign U.S. PPI data all pushed the market in the same direction.
"Market sentiment is just fine. Everybody says we (the Dutch sharemarket) are overbought, but nobody really expects a correction," one dealer said.

After having hovered near its last record closing level for most of the session, Amsterdam's blue chip AEX index got an extra shove from U.S. PPI data over June in late trade, which brought it to a new record close of 936.51, up 11.80 points.
The midcap index also set a record close, ending up 45.11 points at 1,451.66.
The core U.S. producer price index rose 0.1 percent in June, in line with market expectations, and the dollar strengthened against the guilder, edging up to 1.9911 at the end of trade.
Several stocks starred in the overall well-performing market.
"A couple of stocks have been the eye catchers throughout the day," one dealer said.

Financials were well-off, with ABN AMRO closing 1.90 guilders higher at 44.80 guilders after having topped the volume list for most of the session. Rumours it was interested in buying Commercial Union were downplayed by the bank.
"They can call those rumours old stuff, but it's clear something is going on in that stock. Volumes have been far above average the last couple of days," one dealer said.
"The share broke through several resistance levels," another said, adding there was also a run on calls in the stock.
Sector companion Aegon also did well, adding 5.00 guilders to 151.60. "Something is definitely coming up in that stock as well," a third dealer said.
Semiconductor equipment maker ASM Lithography stunned the market, adding over 15 percent to 155.00 guilders.
Dealers said various broker upgrades following a $150 million order announced on Thursday had sparked extreme demand.
"It's a mass-hypnosis, everybody wants the stock," one said.
Software firm Baan tracked ASML, adding 6.20 guilders to 152.70 while Philips - which holds some 25 percent of ASML - climbed 2.60 to 146.70 guilders.
Biochemicals and food group Gistbrocades closed 4.70 guilders higher at 72.60 after ABN AMRO upgraded it to a "buy" and set a share price target of 80.00 guilders.

"We have been very careful with this stock for one year, during which it underperformed the market by almost 50 percent," ABN AMRO analyst David Kerstens said, "but pencillin prices and derivatives seem to be bottoming out and we expect offer and demand to return to balance in the second half of this year."
Feeds company Nutreco, launched in early June, closed up 2.60 guilders at 46.50 as both ABN AMRO and ING Barings had a positive comment on the stock.
